sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Transcontinental Container Block Train Expedited Freight Forwarding

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European/German-Japanese tradition with U.S.-influenced regulatory overlay; cross-strait special legislation governs Mainland Chinese investment)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA, 2010) concluded between the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); provides investment facilitation, trade liberalization, and dispute-cooperation framework
Cross-Strait Agreement on Customs Cooperation (2010, effective 2011) applicable to goods logistics and customs facilitation
Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Strengthening Tax Cooperation (signed 2015, not yet in force; tax planning must assume no DTAA protection)

No formal BIT exists between China and Taiwan as separate contracting parties; mainland investors are protected by the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals applied mutatis mutandis under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法, promulgated 1996, comprehensively amended 2016, latest amendments 2023), Articles 3-14, as the primary AML statute; Counter-Terrorism Financing Act (資恐防制法, 2016); Company Act Article 22-1 (mandatory filing of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of shares with the central competent authority); Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Terrorist Financing for Financial Institutions and Designated Non-Financial Businesses promulgated by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC); Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area (臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例) Article 73 and the Regulations Governing Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area People (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法) requiring pre-approval by the MOEA Investment Commission; financial intelligence unit: Money Laundering Prevention Division, Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (directors, supervisors, and statutory representatives are publicly disclosed via the MOEA commercial registry; beneficial ownership data reported under Company Act Article 22-1 is maintained in government databases accessible to the FIU, tax authorities, and supervisory agencies, but is not placed on the public internet)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Mainland Investor Certificate of Incorporation / Business License (營業執照)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Provincial or municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary office notarization followed by SEF verification (海基會文書驗證); the ROC is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, and PRC apostilles are not recognized by Taiwanese authorities for cross-strait filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Shareholders' Resolution authorizing the Taiwan investment and appointing the local statutory representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Governing board of the mainland investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary office notarization followed by SEF verification (equivalent to consular legalization under the 1993 Cross-Strait Notarial Verification Agreement)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited Financial Statements of the mainland investing company for the most recent fiscal year
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC licensed certified public accountant firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary office notarization followed by SEF verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and domicile evidence of the natural-person UBO (passport or PRC Resident Identity Card copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary office upon verification against public security records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary office notarization followed by SEF verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or capital-contribution payment proof of the mainland investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR or local market regulation bureau / designated custodian bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary office notarization followed by SEF verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, managers, and signatories against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions (applicable to correspondent SWIFT and LC rails), Taiwan FSC-issued watchlists, and the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau's domestic designated-persons list; PEP definition and enhanced due diligence per Article 7 of the Money Laundering Control Act and FSC internal-control regulations; EDD mandated where a UBO or director is a PEP, holds public office in a high-risk jurisdiction, or where trade-based money laundering red flags appear in the rail-freight forwarding model; negative-media checks and cross-verification with mainland corporate registry data required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs National Commercial Administration Portal (經濟部全國商工行政服務入口網), Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review online module — https://gcis.nat.gov.tw
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be composed of traditional Chinese characters and shall be examined under the Regulations Governing Pre-Review of Company Names and Business Scope (公司名稱及業務預查審核準則); an English/romanized trade name may be filed as a supplementary name but does not replace the Chinese statutory name; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name within the same jurisdiction, and the registered business scope must follow the authority's standardized business-scope terminology checklist.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 銀行 (bank) - requires prior FSC approval
保險 (insurance) - requires prior FSC approval
證券 (securities) - requires prior FSC approval
信託 (trust) - requires prior FSC approval
期貨 (futures) - requires prior FSC approval
律師 (lawyer) - requires prior MOJ approval
會計師 (certified public accountant) - requires prior MOF approval
建築師 (architect) - requires prior MOI approval
醫療 / 醫院 (medical / hospital) - requires prior MOHW approval
國營 / 政府 / 中央 (state-run / government / central) - misleading government affiliation
中華民國 / 臺灣 (national-sovereignty sensitive tokens subject to heightened ministerial review and potentially restricted for mainland-invested entities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The approved name and business pre-review is valid for six months from the issuance date; no extension is available, and a fresh pre-review application must be filed after expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written re-review request (複查) with the competent registration authority within fifteen days of service. If the re-review is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (訴願) with the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Administrative Appeal Act within thirty days of service of the re-review denial, followed by an administrative action before the Taipei High Administrative Court if the ministerial appeal is unsuccessful. On-line submission is accepted at the MOEA portal; legal-counsel preparation of the appeal dossier is recommended where the rejection arises from the mainland-investment identity or sensitive-token grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses and commercial agent locations are accepted by the company registry for incorporation filings, provided the address is not a post-office box; however, for the rail-freight forwarding industry, the Investment Commission and practicing banks require a verifiable physical operational address in Taiwan where books, records, and staff are present, and a virtual office alone will materially impair corporate bank-account opening for SWIFT wire and letter-of-credit rails.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate quantified risk: 25-35% probability of at least one unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operation, driven by Investment Commission post-approval monitoring, municipal commerce authority compliance checks, and customs-related trade-based money-laundering inspection pilots targeting logistics intermediaries; an ordinary non-trade service company baseline is 10-15%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name and business-scope pre-review fee (name clearance application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of NT$300 per pre-review application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of mainland investor corporate documents in PRC (certificate of incorporation, board resolution, financial statements, UBO ID evidence - five sets)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Mainland notary fee schedule (RMB 200-500 per document set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SEF cross-strait document verification fees (five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Straits Exchange Foundation (海峽交流基金會)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of NT$300 per verified document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mainland investment permission application fee (陸資來臺投資許可)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee schedule for investment approval applications

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation registration fee (有限公司設立登記)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (authorized commercial registration office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee schedule (base NT$1,000 plus capital-rate component)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and corporate secretarial service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate service provider in Taiwan
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for physical-address and registered-agent services (NT$35,000-40,000 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account pre-arrangement and compliance interview support (SWIFT wire and LC rails)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate services agent / bank compliance facilitation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for account-opening assistance and KYC packaging

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-border corporate legal counsel - structure review, mainland investment approval strategy, UBO piercing, name clearance, and document verification logistics
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained cross-border law firm (Taiwan and PRC qualified counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market phase fee for stage-1 pre-incorporation due diligence and approval filing package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation, courier, and contingency authentication costs (if a Hong Kong intermediate holding route is adopted)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法) — Chapter 3, Articles 98 to 113 (Limited Liability Company), Article 15 (business scope restrictions), Article 387 (filing and registration); Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國投資條例), Articles 6 to 8; Regulations for Company Establishment Registration and Review
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署) — Company and Commerce One-Stop Online Application Platform (公司與商業一站式線上申請作業系統)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: 公司設立登記申請書 (Company Establishment Registration Application Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a limited liability company under the Company Act; however, a foreign-invested company must first obtain approval from the Investment Commission (MOEA), remit the approved subscribed capital into a designated foreign-currency deposit account at an authorized bank, and obtain a certified public accountant's capital verification report prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. All incorporators unanimously ratify the Deed of Incorporation and the foreign-investment approval granted by the Investment Commission. 2. The total subscribed capital of the Company, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, is accepted, and each subscriber's shareholding allocation shall be recorded in the shareholders' register with the capital contribution having been remitted and certified by a certified public accountant. 3. The registered office is fixed at 7F, No. 88, Sec. 1, Zhongxiao E. Rd., Zhongzheng Dist., Taipei; all official notices shall be served at such address. 4. The following officers are appointed: a General Manager with full day-to-day authority, and a responsible person to execute filings. 5. All authorized signatories are directed to complete registration and licensing procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs — Company and Commerce One-Stop Online Application Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name pre-screening application online for a limited liability company (有限公司). A Chinese name, an English romanized name, and the proposed business scope items derived from ISIC 5229 (rail freight intermodal express forwarding, logistics warehousing, and supply-chain management) must be entered. The registry checks for identical or confusingly similar existing corporate names and confirms that the business scope is within the permitted national business items catalogue.
required_dossiers: Online application form for company name reservation
Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft
Identity or incorporation certificate of the foreign investor
Name pre-screening fee remittance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected due to similarity with an existing registration, the applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days, or simply re-submit a new name pre-screening application at no penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the name reservation is approved, the foreign investor files a foreign investment application with the Investment Commission. The application must identify the investment amount, funding source, the business activities (Eurasia container block train expedited forwarding — permitted non-negative-list activity), and the address of the future registered office. The original investment approval letter is a mandatory precondition for capital remittance and company registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certified true copies of the foreign investor's registration or identity documents
Bank references and source-of-funds documentary evidence
Investment plan and projected revenue structure
Articles of Incorporation draft for the future Taiwan entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a request for supplementation, the applicant generally receives a 30-day cure period; one extension of 30 additional days can be requested. In case of substantive rejection, an amended application addressing the stated concerns may be re-filed within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance and Certified Public Accountant Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign-Exchange Bank (指定銀行) authorized to handle foreign currency settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the investment approval letter, open a temporary foreign-currency capital deposit account at an authorized bank, remit the subscribed capital in the original currency, and obtain a foreign exchange settlement certificate. Engage a licensed Taiwan certified public accountant to review the capital contribution and issue a capital verification report (資本額查核報告書), which will be annexed to the establishment registration.
required_dossiers: Original Investment Commission approval letter
Subscription list and share allocation table
Foreign exchange settlement certificate issued by the bank
Bank receipt proving the inward remittance and account balance
CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remitted amount does not match the approved investment amount, the applicant may either file a supplementary investment application or reduce the registered paid-in capital accordingly, followed by a revised CPA verification report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs — Company and Commerce One-Stop Online Application Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company establishment registration application electronically or in person after the capital verification report is issued. Submit the signed Articles of Incorporation, the shareholder list, consent of the registered office landlord, identification documents of the responsible person and manager, and the capital verification report. Upon registration approval, the Ministry of Economic Affairs issues the unified business number (統一編號) and the certificate of company registration; legal personality is effective from the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Signed company establishment registration application
Articles of Incorporation signed by all shareholders
CPA capital verification report
Proof of right to use the registered office (lease or ownership certificate)
National ID or residence permit copies of the shareholders, responsible person and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an amendment notice, corrections must be completed within 15 days; failure to cure results in automatic withdrawal of the application. The applicant may then re-apply with the corrected documents and pay no additional administrative penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Electronic Invoice / VAT Filing Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Taipei Branch, Ministry of Finance (財政部臺北國稅局)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the company registration date, complete the business personality tax registration (營業登記) for the Taipei office and warehouse address. Obtain a value-added tax (VAT) registration certificate and apply for the issuance of electronic invoice (電子發票) uniform-numbers through the e-invoice platform. Register the company's banking accounts and verify withholding obligations for foreign payments under the remittance-based income tax rules.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration certificate (統一編號 certificate)
Approved Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement for the registered office and warehouse
National ID or passport of the responsible person
Bank account certificate opened in the company's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau detects inconsistency between the registered address and actual operation, the taxpayer must correct the registration and may render the e-invoice status temporarily suspended until re-inspection. VAT refunds will resume after the discrepancies are cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Freight Forwarding Business Registration and Warehouse Operation Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Transportation and Communications (交通部) and Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development (for warehouse business registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the rail-intermodal freight expediting activity, apply to the MOTC for the freight forwarding business registration (貨運承攬業登記) by submitting the company registration certificate, operational capability documentation, and an operating plan covering container block-train coordination and customs-bonded transit compliance. Simultaneously, if operating a logistics warehouse in Taipei, submit the logistics-warehousing registration application to the Taipei City Government, which requires the warehouse fire safety inspection certificate and structural safety report. No additional statutory license is required for pure rail-freight arrangement services; the MOTC registration and municipal warehouse approval constitute the full industrial licensing package.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration certificate
Articles of Incorporation with ISIC 5229 related business scope
Warehouse lease or certificate of ownership
Fire safety inspection certificate issued by the Taipei Fire Department
Structural load inspection report for the warehouse racking and flooring system
Operational plan for transcontinental block-train expedited freight forwarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the competent authority raises safety, financial capability or operating-compliance objections, the applicant may submit a rectification plan within 60 days; if accepted, a conditional license with an agreed cure timeline is issued, fully validating after final inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transportation and Communications (交通部) for freight-forwarding registration; Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development and Taipei Fire Department for warehouse physical licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: 貨運承攬業登記證 (Freight Forwarder Registration Certificate) and 物流倉儲登記 (Logistics Warehouse Operation Registration)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (環境部), successor to the Environmental Protection Administration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Fixed Air Pollutant Source Registration required for diesel-powered material-handling equipment and emergency generators; no Full EIA Report required for non-manufacturing logistics warehouse facilities under 6,000 square meters; waste discharge plan registration required for general industrial waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: effluent discharged to public sewer must comply with the Water Pollution Control Act enforcement standards, with BOD ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, and suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L; Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs): forklift and generator emissions must meet stationary-source VOC emission standards set by the Ministry of Environment, with compliance testing every 2 years; Hazardous waste: any incidental hazardous waste (e.g., spent batteries, lubricating oil) must be stored, labeled, and disposed of only through Ministry of Environment licensed waste contractors; Noise: daytime boundary noise ≤ 65 dB(A) and nighttime ≤ 55 dB(A) at the warehouse perimeter; container storage yard drainage must be covered by on-site retention and, where applicable, a discharge permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Taipei Fire Department based on the Fire Services Act (fire-protection equipment inspection, fire-alarm integration, and evacuation drills plan); structural load inspections performed by a licensed structural engineer to certify racking-system, mezzanine and freight-loading-area floor load capacities; and occupational workplace clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act administered by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Ministry of Labor, covering warehouse ventilation, forklift operator training, personal protective equipment, and emergency response plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA). Administratively exercised through the nationwide Unified Electronic Tax Bureau portal (etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and the Comprehensive Digital E-Invoice Platform; export verification is co-administered with the General Administration of Customs via the China International Trade Single Window; foreign exchange monitoring is coordinated with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the 'One License, One Code' (Yi Zhao Yi Ma) reform, the WFOE obtains its statutory tax identification automatically upon issuance of the business license from the Administration for Market Regulation: the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code serves as both the company registration number and the tax ID. Within 30 days after formation, the entity must complete online tax registration confirmation on the Electronic Tax Bureau, activate the tax profile (production and operational taxpayer status), elect general or small-scale VAT taxpayer status, apply for digital invoice quota, and conclude a three-party automatic tax deduction agreement with its bank. Cross-border payments to the Taiwan parent trigger non-resident withholding registration and beneficial ownership documentation for Cross-Strait treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China maintains a per-se entity-level taxation system without check-the-box pass-through or hybrid entity elections. The WFOE is a resident enterprise taxable on worldwide income at 25% CIT. Statutory elections available: (a) general VAT taxpayer status even below the RMB 5,000,000 small-scale threshold, with a 36-month lock-in after election; (b) small low-profit enterprise (small-micro) CIT concession at a 20% reduced rate with an effective 2.5% to 5% burden on qualifying income up to RMB 3,000,000, maximum RMB 50,000,000 total assets and 300 employees (extended by policy to 2027); (c) one-time pre-tax deduction of qualifying fixed assets below RMB 5,000,000; (d) accelerated R&D expense super-deduction election; (e) quarterly prepayment based on actual taxable profit versus an estimated annual installment; (f) application of the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation with the Taiwan administration, including mutual agreement procedure and reduced dividend/interest/royalty withholding; no hybrid mismatch election exists, and thin capitalization (2:1 debt-to-equity) plus transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation rules govern related-party funding.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the new VAT Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 25 December 2024, effective 1 January 2026) replacing the Provisional VAT Regulations and read with CaiShui [2016] No. 36 and the 2017-2019 reform measures; accompanied by urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and local education surcharge on the VAT payable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic entities are VAT-registered from formation under the unified social credit code. The small-scale taxpayer line is annual taxable sales not exceeding RMB 5,000,000; small-scale taxpayers benefit from a levy rate of 3% (temporary reduced to 1% under current policies) and a monthly exemption of up to RMB 100,000 (RMB 300,000 per quarter) on periodic sales. Sectoral headline VAT rates are 13% for goods, 9% for transport and rail-related freight carriage, and 6% for modern services (including freight forwarding agency, logistics ancillary services, and international agency work). A non-resident service supplier without a permanent establishment in China has no fixed local registration threshold: the Chinese resident customer is statutorily required to withhold VAT through reverse charge on payments for taxable services performed by the offshore supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The nationwide Golden Tax Phase IV and Full Digital E-Invoice (Shu Dian Piao) mandate applies. All VAT invoices, including special VAT invoices and export zero-rated invoices, must be created on the STA-controlled e-invoice platform, either through the official browser interface or by application-programming-interface integration of the WFOE's accounting system with the Electronic Tax Bureau. Each invoice carries a unique 20-digit invoice number, an electronic signature/seal, and is cleared in near real-time to the national Golden Tax data warehouse before buyer-side verification is possible. The system performs automatic invoice-to-return-to-tax-declaration reconciliation and risk scoring (governance by data), eliminates physical stamping, requires same-period issuance corresponding to the underlying supply, and flags all export invoices for the joint customs-tax-foreign-exchange matching engine.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT with preservation of input VAT credit/refund) is available to a general VAT taxpayer for: (A) goods physically exported from the PRC customs territory, including rail freight on transcontinental block trains exiting China, where the WFOE is the seller/exporter and the customs export declaration identifies the rail mode of exit; (B) international transportation services involving carriage of goods from a place within China to a place outside China (and the reverse), or between two overseas places, where the WFOE acts as the principal carrier on an international rail journey; and (C) cross-border services wholly consumed outside China, which are zero-rated or exempt under the cross-border taxable services catalogue of CaiShui [2016] No. 36. Pure agency freight forwarding services consumed overseas are VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated unless the WFOE issues the multimodal bill of lading and assumes carrier liability. The claim requires filing the Cross-Border Taxable Services Zero-Rate/Exemption Return on the Electronic Tax Bureau and evidencing the overseas recipient, actual foreign exchange receipt, and the international rail itinerary.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic customs data) evidencing exit of the goods from PRC territory by rail
International Railway Consignment Note (SMGS/CMIS rail waybill) and/or multimodal transport bill of lading issued by the WFOE
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank export foreign exchange collection voucher evidencing receipt from the overseas counterparty
Export sales contract, commercial invoice, and packing list
Special VAT e-invoice for the zero-rated export or cross-border service supply
Cross-Border Taxable Services Zero-Rate/Exemption Declaration (Kua Jing Ying Shui Xing Wei Shi Yong Zeng Zhi Shui Ling Shui Lv Mian Shui Shen Qing Biao) for service-based claims
Export tax rebate application form with supporting customs electronic data matching file
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: All zero-rating and export rebate claims are screened by the joint STA-General Administration of Customs-State Administration of Foreign Exchange data engine and may be subject to documentary verification, on-site inspection, and container-level physical examination. If export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day ceiling, the documentation set is incomplete, the rail waybill and customs data do not reconcile, or the substantive export is not proven, the refund is clawed back with interest and a late-payment surcharge (0.05% per day) and the supply is re-characterized as domestic taxable at the applicable 9% or 6% VAT rate. Fraudulent export rebate claims attract an administrative penalty of 0.5 to 5 times the refunded VAT (Tax Collection Administration Law, Article 63), forfeiture of illegal gains, downgrade of the enterprise tax credit rating to Grade D, suspension or permanent loss of export rebate qualification, inclusion on the joint disciplinary blacklist, and referral to criminal prosecution for fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds (Criminal Law Article 204), which carries imprisonment up to life plus confiscation of property; responsible officers and beneficial owners face parallel individual liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); local SAFE branches supervise and enforce foreign exchange controls on behalf of the PBoC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a managed floating exchange-rate system under which the RMB is fully convertible for current-account items, including trade in goods and services, freight forwarding, logistics fees, and rail transport charges, provided that the underlying transaction is genuine and documentation is retained. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment into a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), shareholder loans, equity transfers, and outward investment, remain subject to SAFE registration, project approval, or filing. For a Taiwan-invested WFOE engaged in ISIC 5229 rail freight and intermodal expediting, inbound capital must be injected through the foreign-currency capital account and may only be converted into RMB for uses consistent with the approved business scope. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder requires completion of the annual statutory audit, corporate income-tax final settlement and tax clearance, a board resolution certifying distributable profits, and a bank-facilitated SAFE profit-remittance procedure. Service-trade remittances, such as payments to overseas railway operators and terminal handlers, are eligible for simplified current-account verification under SAFE rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since SAFE's 2019 reform, China has abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds. All export and service-trade proceeds must be repatriated onshore within statutory time limits: generally 30 days after the service is completed for service trade, and 90 days from customs declaration for goods-related trade, unless a contracting party requires an alternative cash-flow timing. The WFOE may retain such foreign exchange in an onshore current-account balance or convert it to RMB voluntarily. For rail-freight and intermodal expediting services, receipts must be supported by transport contracts, rail waybills, multimodal bills of lading, freight invoices, customs declarations, and the bank's verification of cover under the SAFE current-account transaction-monitoring system. Any retention of export/service proceeds in an offshore account, including under an onward freight-billing model, requires a prior SAFE approval or filing.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs and neobanks holding EU, UK, or Hong Kong licences cannot serve as the primary treasury or settlement account for a mainland China WFOE because they lack a valid Payment Business Licence issued by the PBoC or SAFE. Such EMIs are not permitted to hold RMB, execute domestic payments, or perform tax and statutory fund deposits for the WFOE. They may only perform ancillary collection or cross-border exchange functions through licensed correspondent banks, and even then must use SWIFT/CNAPS gateways with a full AML/KYC trail. The WFOE must open its main operating and capital accounts with a domestically licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated WFOE, the legal representative and, depending on bank policy, at least one director or authorised financial signatory must attend the bank branch in person with original identification documents. Full remote corporate account opening is not generally permitted; some banks allow restricted video-KYC pre-screening, but final verification, seal registration, and UBO interview require a physical visit. Non-resident Taiwan directors unable to travel may be represented under a notarised power of attorney, but the legal representative's in-person interview remains non-waivable. The WFOE must provide proof of registered office, a valid Unified Social Credit Certificate, articles of association, board resolutions, and identification for all natural-person shareholders owning 25% or more.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan shareholder structure and cross-strait ultimate beneficial ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Certificate of Registration of the Taiwan parent; shareholding charts identifying all UBOs; identification of directors and 25% shareholders; board resolution authorising the WFOE's establishment; source-of-funds statement; notarised certification of the Taiwan juridical person; cross-strait investment approvals, including Mainland-Taiwan investment certification and SAFE FDI registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure due to rail route touching, transiting, or terminating in restricted jurisdictions or sanctioned/dual-use cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-risk assessment and end-user certificate; complete rail waybill and cargo manifest; transport contracts and Incoterms; due-diligence file on all counterparties; written compliance assurance that the freight forwarder does not handle embargoed or dual-use goods; bank-specific compliance questionnaire; carriage insurance and customs-release evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity or unexplained cross-border payments to overseas railway operators, terminal handlers, or subcontractors lacking sufficient underlying documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master freight-forwarding agreement or long-term logistics service contract; itemised invoices for each payment; CIM/SMGS consignment notes or multimodal bills; customs declarations; container release orders; detailed audit trail for every SWIFT MT103 outbound and inbound transfer; and periodic SAFE service-trade verification filings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Registered capital from the Taiwan shareholder must be remitted to the WFOE's FDI Capital Account at a licensed domestic bank via SWIFT MT103/MT202 using the SAFE inbound direct-investment purpose code. The remitter must be exactly the Taiwan shareholder named in the approved investment, and the remittance currency may be USD, EUR, RMB, or other major currency. The bank requires the SAFE FDI Registration Certificate or electronic filing number before crediting the capital account. After arrival, funds may be converted into RMB for approved business purposes under the bank's foreign-currency capital-account settlement rules, and surplus conversion requires additional SAFE filing. For Taiwan investment, the applicable registration is under the Mainland-Taiwan investment framework, requiring notarised certification of the Taiwan parent and the Taiwan Compatriots Investment Certificate. A complete verification file must include the audited balance sheet, approved articles of association, business-scope licence, and the SAFE-issued file code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to overseas railway undertakings, terminal operators, feeder carriers, customs brokers, and intermodal subcontractors, the WFOE shall use bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103/MT202 for standard service-trade settlement. High-value or term-based infrastructure and rolling-stock payments above USD 500,000 may be structured under an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (LIC) or standby letter of credit to secure performance and provide negotiable payment assurance to the counterparty. Every payment must be matched to an underlying invoice and transport document, including a rail waybill or multimodal bill. The bank will verify the transaction in the SAFE Service-Trade Exchange / Current-Account Verification system; no customs registration is required when the freight service is rendered independently of goods import/export, unless bundled with goods. To reduce liquidity blockages, the WFOE may implement a centralised international payment factory or RMB/foreign-currency sweeping and netting structure with the lead bank, subject to SAFE treasury-centralisation rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contract (SAFE-approved, underlying current-account exposure in freight billing)
Onshore cross-currency swap (hedging foreign-currency loans and long-term capital-account exposure)
Onshore FX swap (short-term liquidity flexing for cross-border collections and disbursements)

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) - not permissible for direct execution by the onshore WFOE; may be utilised only by the offshore Taiwan parent treasury on a back-to-back basis, with the onshore WFOE's exposure reflected through intercompany re-invoicing and compliant group hedging policies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner and corporate officer information filing (Company Act Art. 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Department of Commerce), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the company's registration anniversary; event-driven update within 15 days of any change in directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding more than 10% of issued shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$50,000–NT$500,000 (approx. US$1,560–US$15,600) per violation; prolonged default may trigger compulsory dissolution by the Ministry of Economic Affairs under Company Act Art. 10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting approval of financial statements and filing to the competent authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (company registry) and shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting held no later than June 30 following the December 31 fiscal year-end; approved financial statements filed with the registry within 15 days of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers subject to fines up to NT$50,000 (approx. US$1,560) per event; persistent non-compliance exposes the company to compulsory dissolution and loss of foreign-investment approval status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual settlement return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by May 31 of the year following the December 31 fiscal year-end (April 1–May 31 filing season); CPA-attested electronic filings may apply for the extended deadline to the end of June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 3% per month on outstanding tax (maximum 9%), plus late-payment interest and penalties; serious or continued failure after demand may lead to estimated assessment, business cessation notice, and administrative strike-off of the corporate registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business operations survey for overseas-Chinese and foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between February 1 and March 31 of each calendar year per the Investment Commission's published survey window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 (approx. US$310–US$1,560) for non-response or false declaration under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, with possible suspension of shareholder-investment approvals

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CPA-attested financial statements are mandatory for companies with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million (approx. US$945,000) under Company Act Art. 228; CPA attestation of the income tax return is required where annual operating revenue exceeds NT$100 million (approx. US$3.15 million) or the tax authority designates certification. Securities issuers are always audited under the Securities and Exchange Act. A low-capital freight-forwarding WFOE below these thresholds is not statutorily required to obtain a full independent audit but must still prepare annual financial statements and maintain books under the Business Entity Accounting Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS (full International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission, effective from January 1, 2013); qualifying private companies may apply TIFRS for SMEs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Company Act Art. 22-1 requires every Taiwan company to report its directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of shares to the MOEA company information platform. The WFOE must file an event-driven update within 15 days after any transfer or change of covered persons and must re-confirm the report annually by the registration anniversary. The annual confirmation must be reconciled with the Register of Members and the minute book before any share transfer is registered.
